content.comment_body: Good evening, could you explain why this message appears?

The message indicates that LSC cannot locate the microSD card. This could be due to multiple reasons. Is the microSD card formatted with FAT32? The maximum accepted size is 32GB. If the card is larger, you need to create a 32GB FAT32 partition. Physical issues might also occur, such as bent pins in the card slot, which is common in older [product_name] modules. This is less frequent with more recent [product_name] versions.
My [product_name] module is new. The microSD is formatted as FAT32 and has 8GB capacity. I can't determine the issue.
Which operating system did you use to format the microSD card?
I was referring to your Windows version—was it Windows 7, 8, 10, or 11?
Do you know anyone with a PC or laptop running an older Windows version, like Windows 7? I always format my microSD cards on a computer with Windows 7.
This is the error description in [product_name] software.
I currently only have a 16GB card available. These are my settings—no quick format used.
Try changing the volume label of the card. Characters like '!' are considered special—use 'logo_sd' or, better yet, leave the label blank.
That may not be accurate. I just formatted a microSD card with the volume label 'SD' and transferring the LWE project to [product_name] worked without issue.
Is the SD card locked? If so, you can’t write data.

Hello, I recall a previous forum post noting that microSD cards from INTENSO often don’t function properly. Try switching to a card from another manufacturer. I use HAMA (8GB), Sandisk (4GB–32GB), and some older microSD cards from [company_name] (4GB & 8GB) with [product_name] modules and they work reliably. All are formatted in Windows 10 to FAT32 with default settings. Hope this advice helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members are facing issues where new [company_name] hardware does not correctly recognize microSD cards formatted to FAT32, even when standard capacity and format recommendations are followed. The problem persists across up-to-date device and software versions, leading to confusion. Discussions highlight that variations in Windows formatting, hardware compatibility, or card brand might be influencing this behavior, but the lack of clear guidance from the manufacturer contributes to user frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect flawless compatibility between [company_name] hardware, its associated software, and microSD cards formatted according to standard FAT32 specifications. They anticipate simply following official recommendations will ensure reliable operation without additional troubleshooting.
